neighbours.label: 'use'/'used' for how long an ancient site or object stayed in use (historical/archaeological prose)
fire: The temple was abandoned in the 9th century, though the road continued to be used for centuries.
The fortress remained in use until the Ottoman conquest.
Archaeologists are still unsure of the original use of these bronze tools.
The aqueduct stayed in use well into the medieval period.
This cemetery was used from the Iron Age until Roman times.
The script fell out of use around 500 BC.
Such stone axes were used by early farmers in the Neolithic.
The harbour went out of use after the river silted up in the 12th century.
quiet: The temple was abandoned in the 9th century, though pilgrims still visited it for centuries.
The fortress was besieged before the Ottoman conquest.
Archaeologists are still studying the decoration of these bronze tools.
The aqueduct was repaired well into the medieval period.
This cemetery dates from the Iron Age to Roman times.
Such stone axes were found near early farming villages of the Neolithic.
The harbour was abandoned after the river silted up in the 12th century.
